lines.text: deliverance. We may have experienced such a thing our-
selves, or if not, we can easily imagine how a person feels
who can breathe again because he has found freedom
from the past which fettered his spirit.
Hence we may perhaps easily understand, in the light of
such human experience, the freedom implied by "that day"
which ultimately frees us from all those things with which
this world binds and burdens us. Does there not steal over us
at times a longing for such freedom? A longing to be cleansed
from all that stains and clouds our being? A longing for a
unity of being through deliverance from all that confuses and
divides our spirit? And that longing which sometimes we
feel for the vanished past of our childhood, with its artless
delights, is it not a longing for freedom from the confusions
of this world?
But do we seriously desire such freedom? We must con-
fess: this freedom is in its roots freedom from ourselves. For
all with which the world exercises its hold over us, good and
ill, pleasure and pain, gains its binding power from ourselves;
from the fact that we have our wishes, our sick desires, our
projects and plans, which the world sometimes meets with
alluring hopes of fulfilment, sometimes crowns with a
measure of success, sometimes severely suppresses and
destroys. It is from the well of our own being that vexing
questions and anxieties arise, because it is we who generate
desires and structures of life. If "that day" is ever to come for
us, the day on which we shall ask no further questions, then
it must come as the day on which our self-will, the motivating
force of our wishes and plans, grows silent; as the day on
which the world for us sinks into nothingness.
But do we wish this? Or should we not rather ask: ought
we to wish it? Do we not stand immersed in this world with
all the obligations of duty too? In relationships which we do
not regard as externally compulsive, but which we joyfully
affirm? Relationships whose binding force springs from our
gifts and endowment? And do we not above all stand in
personal relationships with our own families and friends,
